applies_why: This judge text counts Matthew 1:18 and Matthew 1:25 toward a broken link without quoting an earlier-round sentence pressing them or naming the round.
quote: CHALLENGER LINK BROKEN -- [L1] Matthew 1:18 "before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost" and Matthew 1:25 "knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son" contradict C3's claim of espousal union
rule_words: A verse on a side's 'cited in' line counts as an unanswered witness only when the judge quotes the sentence of the earlier round that pressed it against that link or a listed premise and names that round; a verse cited there but not pressed against the link does not count. A verse the judge counts toward a broken link is counted this way. If the judge says a verse was answered, the judge must not count it. Not counting it obeys this rule.
room: 'A verse the judge counts toward a broken link is counted this way': either any verse used as support for a broken link must satisfy the quote/name requirement, or only verses expressly labeled as cited-in witnesses do.
why: Because the judge treats Matthew 1:18 and Matthew 1:25 as support for the broken C3 link but does not quote an earlier-round pressing sentence or name any round, it counts them contrary to K-G4.
